set.rappels: Usually 3 rappels down the summit pyramid's central gully (two to four by snow cover), from webbing anchors with rap rings; a 60 m rope reaches all stations
set.descent_text: Descend the same line: reverse the Sulphide Glacier back to camp, then the Shannon Ridge Trail back to the trailhead. Off the summit, the standard descent down the central gully of the summit pyramid is a mix of downclimbing and rappelling. NPS climbing rangers have reported parties periodically replacing worn rap rings and anchors in the gully, so expect a mix of fixed rings/webbing at established stations supplemented by natural anchors (slung horns) rather than bolted hardware throughout. Plan on roughly two to four rappels depending on snow coverage and season — more rock is exposed and more rappels are typically needed later in the season, while early-season snow often lets parties downclimb and plunge-step more and rappel less. A 60m rope reaches between all standard stations; a 30m works but requires linking some sections with downclimbing between anchors. Note that stations are generally spaced for ropes with normal stretch — thin static or RAD-line-style ropes may leave gaps that require short, unprotected downclimbs between anchors. When the gully is dry and snow-free (typically later in summer), some parties instead descend the Southeast Ridge (about 5.3 with selective route-finding, or 5.6-5.7 held strictly to the crest) as a scramble alternative that avoids rappelling — but this is sustained 4th- to mid-5th-class terrain, not a simple walk-off, and isn't always in condition. Once back on the Sulphide Glacier, re-rope for glacier travel and retrace the ascent track to camp, watching for softened or newly opened crevasses in the afternoon.
